pages.t: jq for YAML -- query and edit without reformatting
pages.l: A jq-style query and editing tool for YAML: reads give back your own bytes, edits change only what you name.
All notable changes to yqr are documented here. The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and the project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

pages.t: How yqr compares to other YAML tools
pages.l: Where yqr differs from the YAML tools you already have, measured against real files rather than argued.

pages.t: yqr and yq -- which tool for which job
pages.l: Two YAML tools with overlapping surfaces and different jobs. Here is what each one is good at, measured rather than argued.
A runnable script that walks yqr's query, edit, and validate surface against sample files you can inspect afterwards.
Where to start: installing yqr, byte-for-byte reads, surgical edits, validation, enumeration, and arriving from jq.

pages.t: Enumerating a mapping without losing the keys
pages.l: How to report what each entry of a mapping is about, with `to_entries`, when iterating throws the keys away.
Why `yqr '.' f` reproduces `f` exactly, what survives a read, and when you want `--normalize` instead.
Most of your jq muscle memory works unchanged. Here is the part that transfers, the one habit to unlearn, and where the two languages stop.
Homebrew, a shell installer, `cargo install`, or a prebuilt archive you verify yourself -- and how to confirm the binary works.

pages.t: Editing Kubernetes manifests without reformatting them
pages.l: How to bump an image tag or a replica count so the diff is one line, and which edits yqr refuses outright.

pages.t: Validating YAML from the command line
pages.l: How to check a file is still correct after an edit, what each exit code means, how duplicate keys are reported, and how to validate against a JSON Schema.
The same engine as the CLI, compiled to WebAssembly, running in your browser. Type a filter, edit the document, and watch exactly which bytes an edit touches.
